beats.text: In 1861, Harriet Colfax took charge of Michigan City's lighthouse. She kept the light burning for 43 years.
beats.label: MICHIGAN CITY, INDIANA

beats.text: She lived in the lighthouse with her lifelong companion, Ann Hartwell.
beats.label: HARRIET AND ANN

beats.text: Every night of the shipping season, she lit the lights after sunset.
beats.label: AFTER SUNSET

beats.text: After 1871, she also walked a long, raised walkway out the pier to a second light, even when ice coated the walk.
beats.label: OUT THE PIER

beats.text: In 1873, she wrote in her log: A terrible hurricane tonight.
beats.label: HER LOG, 1873
beats.credit: National Park Service; Indiana State Library

beats.text: Harriet retired in 1904, at about 80. She died the next spring.
beats.credit: Lighthousefriends; Indiana State Library; National Park Service

beats.text: Her 1858 lighthouse still stands. It's been a museum since 1973, open April through October.
beats.label: THE OLD LIGHTHOUSE
beats.credit: Michigan City Historical Society; Lighthousefriends; Indiana Landmarks

beats.text: Comment your town, and it could be next.

factcheck.result: All dates supported. 'Every night' became 'every night of the shipping season' (lights, plural); 'catwalk' became 'raised walkway'; museum season named (April-October) since it closed Oct. 31; the 1904 pierhead tower drawing replaced by a plain pier (her 1871 light was a wooden tower).
